item.title: 疾病的自然史：預後表示法
item.description:
疾病的自然史：預後表示法

原文章節： The Natural History of Disease: Ways of Expressing Prognosis

📚 學習目標

  • To compare ive different ways of describing the natural history of disease: case-fatality, ive-year survival, observed survival, median survival time, and relative survival.
  • To describe two approaches for calculating observed survival over time: the life table approach and the Kaplan-Meier method.
  • To illustrate the use of life tables for examining changes in survival.
  • To describe how improvements in available diagnostic methods may affect the estimation of prognosis (stage migration).

內容概要

At this point, we have learned how diagnostic and screening tests permit the categorization of sick and healthy individuals. Once a person is identiied as having a disease, the question arises, “How can we characterize the natural history of the disease in quantitative terms?” Such quantiication is impor- tant for several reasons. First, it is necessary to describe the severity of a disease to establish priori- ties for clinical services and public health programs. Second, patients often ask questions about progno- sis (Fig. 6-1). Third, such quantiication is impor- tant to establish a baseline for natural history, so that as new treatments become available, the effects of these treatments can be compared with the expected outcome without them. Furthermore, if different types of therapy are available for a given disease, such as surgical or medical treatments or two different types of surgical procedures, we want to be able to compare the effectiveness of the various types of therapy. Therefore, to allow such a comparison, we need a quantitative means of expressing the prognosis in groups receiving differ- ent treatments.
